source.title: Multi-Agent Verification: Scaling Test-Time Compute with Multiple Verifiers
source.authors: Shalev Lifshitz; Sheila A. McIlraith; Yi-Lun Du

page_placements.theme: Weaker or smaller verifiers and reward models improve a stronger generator through test-time selection (reranking, best-of-N)

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper invokes weak-to-strong generalization and uses weaker verifiers to improve stronger generators, but its intervention is test-time candidate selection, not fine-tuning on labels from a weaker supervisor or measuring PGR.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports results for weaker aspect verifiers used in BoN-MAV, but these are test-time selection results, not fine-tuning results. The authors explicitly say they did not investigate fine-tuning the generator on MAV-selected outputs. The Table 2 results are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not measure a version's specified fine-tuning behavior or PGR. Other comparisons of MAV, reward-model verification, self-consistency, and verifier-count scaling concern the paper's test-time method rather than the claimed fine-tuning intervention.
record.test_reason: The paper uses the label 'weak-to-strong generalization' for test-time best-of-n selection: weaker prompted verifiers vote among a stronger generator's samples. No model is fine-tuned on weak labels, no strong ceiling is trained, and no PGR is computed. The authors say they 'did not investigate finetuning the generator LLM' (Section 4). This is neither a test of the claim nor a use of the finding as a tool, so T6/discusses fits better than the reader's T4/uses_without_test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors conclude that scaling the number of verifiers is a promising test-time dimension, and that BoN-MAV improves performance across domains and generators. They say it 'enables weak-to-strong generalization', meaning weak verifiers improve stronger generators at test time, and that it enables self-improvement. Fine-tuning on MAV-selected outputs is left to future work.
record.recipe_differences: BoN-MAV samples candidate outputs and selects among them by votes from prompted aspect verifiers at inference time. It does not fine-tune on weak labels or report PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Test-time gains vary by generator model and domain; the paper also reports domain-dependent verifier subsets and variation as verifier count changes.

fits_no_version.finding: Test-time BoN-MAV, with verifiers built on weaker models (Gemini-1.5-Flash, GPT-4o-mini), raises the accuracy of stronger generators over pass@1 on most domains. Gemini-1.5-Pro gains 64.7 to 72.7 on MATH. GPT-4o drops 94 to 92 on HumanEval.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weaker LLM verifiers combined by voting can improve a stronger generator's accuracy through test-time selection, varying by task.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-verification with same-model aspect verifiers improves pass@1 on all domains except HumanEval, for Gemini-1.5-Flash and GPT-4o-mini.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-time self-verification with multiple prompted verifiers from the same model improves accuracy, except on coding.

record.problems: The weak-to-strong results are test-time accuracy comparisons, not fine-tuning experiments or PGR measurements. Table 2 gives no uncertainty estimates. The paper reports spread across verifier combinations in Figure 5, and domain-specific verifier sets are selected using validation performance.
record.rows_left_out: No other results are included as rows because they report MAV test-time scaling or method comparisons rather than the weak-label fine-tuning claim. The paper states in Section 4 that fine-tuning on outputs selected by MAV was not investigated.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning a strong model on weak labels; PGR against a strong ceiling.
Training changes to weak-label fine-tuning (auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling, loss variants).
PGR dependence on supervisor and student size, task or representations under weak-label training.
Exploitation of the weak supervisor, distribution shift, correlated errors in weak-to-strong training.

record.verdict_notes: The reader grouped all 16 Table 2 rows as weak-to-strong. Only the Gemini-1.5-Pro and GPT-4o rows are weak-to-strong; the Gemini-1.5-Flash and GPT-4o-mini rows are self-improvement with same-model verifiers. The weak-to-strong rows use verifier subsets selected on validation performance across generators, which favours these results. 'Weak-to-strong' here is a terminological borrowing from Burns et al., not the training-based phenomenon.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning a strong model on labels from a weaker model and PGR are not tested; the paper uses test-time verifier voting.
No training changes to weak-label fine-tuning are tested.
The paper varies generator models and tasks for test-time verification, but does not measure PGR or its dependence on size, task, or representations under weak-label fine-tuning.
No weak-label fine-tuning failure modes or PGR under distribution shift or correlated errors are tested.
No theory about students beating weak supervisors is tested.

relation.reason: The authors discuss Burns et al. and describe weaker verifiers improving stronger generators, while leaving fine-tuning on selected outputs to future work.

tranche.reason: BoN-MAV measures test-time selection accuracy without weak-label fine-tuning or PGR; it neither tests nor uses the catalog's training finding.

source_check.notes: The numerical statement is accurate. These results belong among off-claim examples; the paper's weak-to-strong terminology refers to inference-time verification.
